Calculate measures of latent VAR community stability

Source: R/stability.R
stability.mvgam.Rd

Compute reactivity, return rates and contributions of interactions to stationary forecast variance from mvgam models with Vector Autoregressive dynamics.

Usage

stability(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
stability(
  object,
  groups = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
  future = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class mvgam fitted with a VAR(p = 1) latent process model

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

groups

Hierarchical VAR fits only. The panels to summarise, by name or by index into the levels of gr. The default NULL summarises every panel. A non-hierarchical fit accepts NULL alone.

ndraws

Positive integer specifying number of posterior draws to use. NULL (default) uses all available draws.

draw_ids

Optional integer vector selecting a subset of posterior draw indices to use. NULL (default) uses all draws (subject to ndraws).

summary

Logical. TRUE (the default) returns the posterior median and interval of each metric. FALSE returns the metrics of each draw. plot() draws histograms of either form.

probs

The lower and upper percentiles of the interval reported with the median when summary = TRUE.

future

Logical. When TRUE, the per-draw computation runs under the future::plan() the caller has set. The default sequential plan runs as base lapply() does. plan(multisession, workers = N) splits the draws across N R processes. Without the future package the draws run in turn, with a message.

Value

A data.frame with the posterior median and interval of each stability metric, or under summary = FALSE an object of class mvgam_stability holding one row of metrics per posterior draw.

Details

These measures describe how much the lagged interactions among the series contribute to the variability of the system. They also describe how the system responds to a perturbation (Ives et al. 2003). For a latent VAR(1)

$$ x_t \sim \text{MVNormal}(A x_{t - 1}, \Sigma) $$

the stationary covariance \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) solves \(\Sigma_{\infty} = A \Sigma_{\infty} A^\top + \Sigma\). Each posterior draw of \(A\) and \(\Sigma\) gives one draw of every metric:

  • prop_int: the proportion of the volume of the stationary distribution that the lagged interactions generate, \(\det(A)^2\).

    \item `prop_int_adj`: `prop_int` scaled by the number of series
\eqn{p}, \eqn{|\det(A)|^{2/p}}. It compares across systems of
different size.

\item `prop_int_offdiag`, `prop_int_diag`: the sensitivity of
`prop_int` to each cell of \eqn{A} is
\eqn{2 \det(A) (A^{-1})^\top}. `prop_int_offdiag` is the mean
absolute sensitivity of the off-diagonal cells (interactions
between series) as a share of that mean plus the mean absolute
sensitivity of the diagonal cells (self-regulation).
`prop_int_diag` is the remaining share.

\item `prop_cov_offdiag`, `prop_cov_diag`: the same split for the
sensitivity of \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})} to each cell of
\eqn{\Sigma_{\infty}}, \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})
    (\Sigma_{\infty}^{-1})^\top}. Off-diagonal cells are counted
where \eqn{\Sigma} is estimated.

\item `reactivity`: the log of the largest singular value of
\eqn{A}, \eqn{\log \sigma_{max}(A)} (Neubert et al. 2009). A
positive value means some perturbation grows in the step after
it occurs, before the system returns to equilibrium.

\item `mean_return_rate`: the largest modulus of the eigenvalues
of \eqn{A}. The distance of the mean from its stationary value
shrinks by this factor each step, asymptotically. A value nearer
1 means a slower return.

\item `var_return_rate`: the same factor for the variance, the
largest modulus of the eigenvalues of \eqn{A \otimes A}, which
is `mean_return_rate` squared.

The prior on \(A\) keeps every draw stationary (Heaps 2023). \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) and every metric then exist in every draw.

irf() and fevd() describe the same dynamics as responses to shocks.

References

AR Ives, B Dennis, KL Cottingham & SR Carpenter (2003). Estimating community stability and ecological interactions from time-series data. Ecological Monographs, 73, 301-330.

MG Neubert, H Caswell & AR Solow (2009). Detecting reactivity. Ecology, 90, 2683-2688.

SE Heaps (2023). Enforcing stationarity through the prior in vector autoregressions. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 32, 74-83.

See also

irf() and fevd() summarise the same VAR dynamics. The VAR article runs stability() on a plankton community. The hierarchical VAR article reports the metrics for each group of a hierarchical VAR.

Other latent dynamics: active_factors(), compare_loadings(), fevd.mvgam(), irf.mvgam(), ordinate(), posterior_transition_matrix(), residual_cor(), shared_variation()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(0)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = gaussian(), n_series = 3L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = VAR(),
                    prop_trend = 0.95)
var_mod <- mvgam(y ~ 1, trend_formula = ~ VAR(p = 1),
                 data = simdat$data_train, family = gaussian(),
                 chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 44 of 2000 (2.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 1 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Posterior medians and intervals of the stability metrics
stab <- stability(var_mod)
stab[stab$metric %in% c("reactivity", "mean_return_rate"), ]
#>             metric    Estimate Est.Error       Q2.5     Q97.5
#> 7       reactivity -0.06752746 0.1284961 -0.2841517 0.7699353
#> 8 mean_return_rate  0.82382811 0.0735674  0.6710897 0.9331748

# The full posterior of each metric
plot(stability(var_mod, summary = FALSE))


# Next: irf() traces a shock through the system over time
# }
